approach: Teach el, la, los and las, the contractions al and del, and the places Spanish uses an article where English does not: general statements, titles when talking about someone, days, and languages as a subject.
coverage: el (masc. sing.), la (fem. sing.), los (masc. pl.), las (fem. pl.)
a + el = al; de + el = del
General statements use the article: El café es caro. La salud es importante.
A title takes the article when you talk about someone: La doctora Ruiz es de Perú
No article when you speak to them: Buenos días, doctora Ruiz
Days take el for "on": el lunes
Languages: El español es fácil, but Hablo español (no article after hablar)

data.anchor: Spanish uses el, la, los or las in several places where English uses no article at all.
prerequisites: Things in general: El café es caro. (Coffee is expensive.)
Abstract ideas: La salud es importante. (Health is important.)
A title, when you talk about someone: La doctora Ruiz es de Perú.
Days, for "on": El lunes voy al banco. (On Monday I go to the bank.)
A language as the subject: El español es bonito.

data.question: How do you say "the teacher's car" (the car of the teacher, el profesor)?

trapReasons.1: It follows "of the" word for word.

data.whyIntuitionFailed: Like a + el, de + el looks like two separate words in English.
data.correctReasoning: de + el always fuses into del: el carro del profesor. With la nothing fuses: la casa de la profesora.
data.recoveryTip: a + el = al, de + el = del.

blocks.purpose: Closes with the four articles and the extra places they appear.

data.takeaway: El, la, los, las (plus al and del) appear in general statements, with titles when talking about someone, with days and with languages as a subject.

checks.prompt: Which is the natural Spanish for "Health is important"?
checks.rationale: A general or abstract noun as the subject takes the article in Spanish: La salud.
checks.hint: Spanish uses the article for ideas in general.

checks.prompt: You are telling a friend about your neighbor, Mr. Gómez. Which sentence is correct?
checks.answer: El señor Gómez es de Cuba.
checks.rationale: Talking about someone with a title, Spanish uses the article: el señor Gómez.
checks.hint: You are talking about him, not to him.
choices: El señor Gómez es de Cuba.
Un señor Gómez es de Cuba.
Los señor Gómez es de Cuba.

checks.prompt: Combine and type the one word for "a + el".
checks.rationale: a + el always contracts to al, as in voy al banco.
